title: ChAI-Net learns a regulatory code for chromatin co-accessibility
summary: Identifies distinct sequence motifs and motif arrangement/orientation patterns associated with co-accessibility at enhancers, promoters and CTCF-bound regions in mouse embryonic stem cells, including patterns missed by average-accessibility modeling. Held-out test set (MSE 0.0079; Pearson r=0.46) plus in-silico motif insertion/ablation; no direct experimental perturbation validation reported in the results.
ai_technology: Deep convolutional neural network predicts chromatin co-accessibility maps from DNA sequence; interpretation provides motif-level regulatory hypotheses.

source_review.scope: Read the full bioRxiv v1 preprint in PMC (2026-10-31). Methods/Results show ChAI-Net is a deep CNN trained on ~3.4 million 2,048-bp windows of mouse embryonic stem-cell SAMOSA single-molecule footprint data to predict 16-bp-resolution co-accessibility maps. Held-out testing reports MSE 0.0079 and Pearson r=0.46; model interpretation and in-silico motif insertion/ablation identify sequence motifs and spacing/orientation patterns associated with co-accessibility, including patterns not recovered by average-accessibility modeling. This is a new, model-derived regulatory finding, with validation limited to held-out data and computational perturbations in one cell context (not causal wet-lab perturbation). The full text identifies Version 1 dated 2026-10-31 as containing the result. Exact DOI and title were checked and are absent from the active and archived catalog snapshots.
